### <a name="networkmanager"></a>`networkmanager`

This is main class of the network manager puppet module and
you can define here nm module behaviour setting up parameters:

#### Examples

##### 

```puppet

```

##### <a name="-networkmanager--erase_unmanaged_keyfiles"></a>`erase_unmanaged_keyfiles`

Data type: `Boolean`

If you want to remove puppet unmanaged keyfiles (*.nmconnection) from the $connections_dir directory DEFAULT: false

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--connections_dir"></a>`connections_dir`

Data type: `Stdlib::Absolutepath`

the directory with the connection keyfiles DEFAULT: /etc/NetworkManager/system-connections

Default value: `'/etc/NetworkManager/system-connections'`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--no_auto_default"></a>`no_auto_default`

Data type: `Boolean`

If you want to add no-auto-default=* option inside main /etc/NetworkManager/NetworkManager.conf config file. DEFAULT: false
(only the wildcard is supported, use the $additional_config for a list of devices)

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--install_package"></a>`install_package`

Data type: `Boolean`

Install the NetworkManager package (the OS package manager is used) DEFAULT: true

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ignore_unsupported_os"></a>`ignore_unsupported_os`

Data type: `Boolean`

do not fail on an operating system family the module has no package name for, the package is not managed then
(install NetworkManager by other means) DEFAULT: false

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--version"></a>`version`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

version string for NetworkManager version you want to install

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--unmanaged_devices"></a>`unmanaged_devices`

Data type: `Array[Networkmanager::Unmanaged_device]`

Array of the devices you want the NetworkManager to ignore (as name or mac address, you can mix it)

Default value: `[]`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--wait_online"></a>`wait_online`

Data type: `Boolean`

enable the NetworkManager-wait-online service DEFAULT: true, false stops and disables it on systemd hosts and leaves other service managers alone

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--use_internal_resolv_conf"></a>`use_internal_resolv_conf`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[Boolean, Enum['stub']]]`

use the networkmanager bundled resolver

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--plugins"></a>`plugins`

Data type: `Array[Networkmanager::Plugin]`

should we use different plugins to get network config data (NOT RECOMMENDED TO CHANGE)

Default value: `['keyfile']`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--max_length_of_connection_id"></a>`max_length_of_connection_id`

Data type: `Integer[3]`

Limit the name of the connection to this length. DEFAULT: 15 characters
to comply with kernel interface name limits since the connection $id is used as default
for the connection $interface_name, if you change this you need to take care to supply
the $interface_name with length < 16 characters where applicable

Default value: `15`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--duid_prefix"></a>`duid_prefix`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A\h{2}(:\h{2}){3}\z/]`

allows the change of the duid prefix to anything other with format "aa:bb:cc:dd" (downcased)

Default value: `'00:03:00:01'`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ipv6_dhcp_duid_default"></a>`ipv6_dhcp_duid_default`

Data type: `Networkmanager::DHCP_DUID`

the IPv6 DHCP DUID used for the connections which do not set their own $ipv6_dhcp_duid DEFAULT: 'auto'
'auto' builds it from the mac address of the connection (the connection needs the $mac_address), 'unset' writes nothing so NetworkManager
uses its own default, the NetworkManager keywords (ll, llt, lease, stable-ll, stable-llt, stable-uuid) or a literal DUID (aa:bb:cc:...) are used as they are

Default value: `'auto'`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--show_diff"></a>`show_diff`

Data type: `Boolean`

show the diffs of the keyfiles and of the NetworkManager.conf when they change (with the secrets censored, and only when the
`show_diff` setting of Puppet is enabled as it is for the file resource) DEFAULT: true

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--secret_keys"></a>`secret_keys`

Data type: `Array[String]`

names of the settings whose values are censored in the diffs in addition to the built in ones (passwords, psk, wep keys,
private keys, everything in the vpn-secrets section, ...) DEFAULT: []. A name matches every setting that contains it (case insensitive),
so `key` censors all the settings with `key` in the name

Default value: `[]`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--additional_config"></a>`additional_config`

Data type: `Hash`

Configuration hash for the NetworkManager.conf, it is able to override default module config in case of conflict!

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--uuid_seed"></a>`uuid_seed`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

the text the UUIDs of the connections are derived from together with their ids, DEFAULT: the certname of the node (the fqdn fact without it).
Set it to keep the UUIDs when the node gets another certname (a reinstall), or to give the same connection the same UUID on more nodes.

Default value: `undef`

### <a name="networkmanager--config"></a>`networkmanager::config`

This class configures file /etc/NetworkManager/NetworkManager.conf (the networkmanager_keyfile resource),
sets up whether to erase unmanaged keyfiles, and adds no-auto-default option
inside config file according to no_auto_default parameter defined at the entrance
of networkmanager class.
It is not recommended to use it without main networkmanager class.

### <a name="networkmanager--connection_link"></a>`networkmanager::connection_link`

This defined resource keeps the link of the device of a connection down when the connection has the state 'down',
or lets NetworkManager manage the device when it has the state 'up'.
NetworkManager leaves the link administratively UP after the connection is deactivated (or when it was never
activated), so the link is shut down explicitly. The provider of networkmanager_link does it persistently and unmanages
the device with `nmcli device set <ifc> managed --permanent down` when NetworkManager supports it, with `ip link`
otherwise. Bringing it back is done by switching the state to 'up', the device is then managed again before the
connection is activated. The title is the UUID of the connection.
It should not be used by user

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `networkmanager::connection_link` defined type:

* [`state`](#-networkmanager--connection_link--state)
* [`ensure`](#-networkmanager--connection_link--ensure)
* [`interface_name`](#-networkmanager--connection_link--interface_name)
* [`mac_address`](#-networkmanager--connection_link--mac_address)

##### <a name="-networkmanager--connection_link--state"></a>`state`

Data type: `Enum['up', 'down']`

the state of the connection

##### <a name="-networkmanager--connection_link--ensure"></a>`ensure`

Data type: `Enum['absent', 'present']`

'absent' means the connection is removed: the device is given back to NetworkManager (managed), nothing else is ordered

Default value: `'present'`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--connection_link--interface_name"></a>`interface_name`

Data type: `Optional[Networkmanager::Interface_name]`

the name of the device, this or the $mac_address is required

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--connection_link--mac_address"></a>`mac_address`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::MAC]`

the MAC address of the device

Default value: `undef`

### <a name="networkmanager--connection_manage"></a>`networkmanager::connection_manage`

This defined resource manages one connection: it checks the id, writes the keyfile, activates (or deactivates, or
removes) the connection, keeps the link of its device in the state of the connection and collects the activation
execs. It is the common part of all the networkmanager::ifc::* defined resources, which only build the content
of the keyfile. The title is the id of the connection.
It should not be used by user

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `networkmanager::connection_manage` defined type:

* [`content`](#-networkmanager--connection_manage--content)
* [`ensure`](#-networkmanager--connection_manage--ensure)
* [`state`](#-networkmanager--connection_manage--state)
* [`after`](#-networkmanager--connection_manage--after)
* [`interface_name`](#-networkmanager--connection_manage--interface_name)
* [`mac_address`](#-networkmanager--connection_manage--mac_address)

##### <a name="-networkmanager--connection_manage--content"></a>`content`

Data type: `Hash`

The keyfile as a hash of the sections, it has to hold the `connection.uuid`, which is used to activate the connection

##### <a name="-networkmanager--connection_manage--ensure"></a>`ensure`

Data type: `Enum['absent', 'present']`

state of the interface config DEFAULT: present

Default value: `present`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--connection_manage--state"></a>`state`

Data type: `Enum['up', 'down']`

state of the interface (UP/DOWN) not relevant when $ensure == 'absent' DEFAULT: 'up'

Default value: `'up'`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--connection_manage--after"></a>`after`

Data type: `Array[Pattern[/\A\h{8}-(\h{4}-){3}\h{12}\z/]]`

UUIDs of the connections (master, parent) which are activated before this one when they are managed by this module

Default value: `[]`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--connection_manage--interface_name"></a>`interface_name`

Data type: `Optional[Networkmanager::Interface_name]`

name of the device of the connection, the link of the device is kept in the state of the connection (with the $mac_address)

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--connection_manage--mac_address"></a>`mac_address`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::MAC]`

MAC address of the device of the connection

Default value: `undef`

```puppet
      '802.3ad',
      'balance-tlb',
      'balance-alb'
    ]
  ]
```

bonding mode DEFAULT: 'balance-rr'

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ifc--bond--ipv4_address"></a>`ipv4_address`

Data type: `Optional[Networkmanager::IPV4_ADDRESSES]`

the IPv4 address with the prefix length and an optional gateway (192.0.2.12/24 or 192.0.2.12/24,192.0.2.1), more addresses as an array or as a string separated by a semicolon (192.0.2.12/24;198.51.100.12/24)

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ifc--bond--ipv4_gateway"></a>`ipv4_gateway`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::IP::Address::V4::Nosubnet]`

the IPv4 gateway for the connection

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ifc--bond--ipv4_dns"></a>`ipv4_dns`

Data type: `Optional[Networkmanager::DNS_IPV4]`

up to 5 DNS servers for the IPv4: an array of addresses or a string with the addresses separated by a semicolon (192.0.2.53;192.0.2.54;)

Default value: `undef`

Data type: `Boolean`

is it OK that the IPv4 config fails? DEFAULT: true

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ifc--bond--ipv6_method"></a>`ipv6_method`

Data type: `Enum['auto','dhcp','manual','ignore','link-local','disabled']`

what method to use to get an ipv6 address DEFAULT: 'auto'

Default value: `'auto'`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ifc--bond--ipv6_address"></a>`ipv6_address`

Data type: `Optional[Networkmanager::IPV6_ADDRESSES]`

the IPv6 address with the prefix length (2001:db8::12/64), more addresses as an array or as a string separated by a semicolon (2001:db8::12/64;2001:db8:1::12/64)

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ifc--bond--ipv6_gateway"></a>`ipv6_gateway`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::IP::Address::V6::Nosubnet]`

the ipv6 gateway for the connection

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ifc--bond--ipv6_dns"></a>`ipv6_dns`

Data type: `Optional[Networkmanager::DNS_IPV6]`

up to 5 DNS servers for the IPv6: an array of addresses or a string with the addresses separated by a semicolon (2001:db8::53;2001:db8::54;)

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ifc--bond--ipv6_dhcp_duid"></a>`ipv6_dhcp_duid`

Data type: `Optional[Networkmanager::DHCP_DUID]`

IPv6 DHCP DUID, 'auto' builds it from the $mac_address, 'unset' writes nothing (NetworkManager default), a NetworkManager keyword or a literal DUID is used as it is DEFAULT: $networkmanager::ipv6_dhcp_duid_default

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ifc--bond--ipv6_addr_gen_mode"></a>`ipv6_addr_gen_mode`

Data type: `Integer[0, 3]`

IPv6 method for generating of the automatic interface address (0 eui64, 1 stable-privacy, 2 default-or-eui64, 3 default) DEFAULT: 0, the address stays the same, a deliberate choice for servers

Default value: `0`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ifc--bond--ipv6_privacy"></a>`ipv6_privacy`

Data type: `Integer[-1, 2]`

IPv6 privacy extensions (temporary addresses: -1 default, 0 disabled, 1 prefer public, 2 prefer temporary) DEFAULT: 0, a deliberate choice for servers

Default value: `0`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ifc--bond--ipv6_may_fail"></a>`ipv6_may_fail`

Data type: `Boolean`

is it OK that the ipv6 config fails? DEFAULT: true

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ifc--bond--additional_config"></a>`additional_config`

Data type: `Hash`

Other not covered configuration
In the case when you want to specify special not listed parameters you can add them through
$additional_config hash and it will be merged with other parameters.
The additional_config has the HIGHEST priority when merged!
ie: it will override the defined values of the connection in case of the conflict
A setting with an empty string value ('') is not written, like an unset one; the connection.id, uuid, interface-name, master and slave-type can not be overridden

Default value: `{}`

### <a name="networkmanager--ifc--fallback"></a>`networkmanager::ifc::fallback`

This defined resource creates the user defined connection keyfile.
Notes:
  This resource supplies some, hopefully sane, defaults you can override in the $config parameter
  connection.uuid = generated by the module unless it is already an uuid
  connection.type = DEFAULT: ethernet
  ethernet.auto-negotiate = true
  ipv4.method = auto
  ipv6.method = auto
WARNING:
  The name of master or parent are translated to uuid unless they are provided as uuids!
  You can not override this behaviour.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `networkmanager::ifc::fallback` defined type:

* [`config`](#-networkmanager--ifc--fallback--config)
* [`ensure`](#-networkmanager--ifc--fallback--ensure)
* [`state`](#-networkmanager--ifc--fallback--state)
* [`id`](#-networkmanager--ifc--fallback--id)
* [`interface_name`](#-networkmanager--ifc--fallback--interface_name)
* [`mac_address`](#-networkmanager--ifc--fallback--mac_address)

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ifc--fallback--config"></a>`config`

Data type: `Hash`

The definition of the connection REQUIRED

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ifc--fallback--ensure"></a>`ensure`

Data type: `Enum['absent', 'present']`

state of the interface config DEFAULT: present

Default value: `present`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ifc--fallback--state"></a>`state`

Data type: `Enum['up', 'down']`

state of the interface (UP/DOWN) not relevant when $ensure == 'absent' DEFAULT: 'up'

Default value: `'up'`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ifc--fallback--id"></a>`id`

Data type: `String`

the name of the connection DEFAULT: $title of the resource

Default value: `$title`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ifc--fallback--interface_name"></a>`interface_name`

Data type: `Optional[Networkmanager::Interface_name]`

name of the device of the connection, needed only to keep its link in the state of the connection (it is not written to the keyfile,
set the connection.interface-name in the $config for it)

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ifc--fallback--mac_address"></a>`mac_address`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::MAC]`

MAC address of the device of the connection, the same use as the $interface_name (it is not written to the keyfile)

Default value: `undef`

Data type: `Optional[Networkmanager::DHCP_DUID]`

IPv6 DHCP DUID, 'auto' builds it from the $mac_address, 'unset' writes nothing (NetworkManager default), a NetworkManager keyword or a literal DUID is used as it is DEFAULT: $networkmanager::ipv6_dhcp_duid_default

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ifc--vlan--ipv6_addr_gen_mode"></a>`ipv6_addr_gen_mode`

Data type: `Integer[0, 3]`

IPv6 method for generating of the automatic interface address (0 eui64, 1 stable-privacy, 2 default-or-eui64, 3 default) DEFAULT: 0

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ifc--vlan--ipv6_privacy"></a>`ipv6_privacy`

Data type: `Integer[-1, 2]`

IPv6 privacy extensions (-1 default, 0 disabled, 1 prefer public, 2 prefer temporary) DEFAULT: 0

Default value: `0`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ifc--vlan--ipv6_may_fail"></a>`ipv6_may_fail`

Data type: `Boolean`

is it OK that the ipv6 config fails? DEFAULT: true

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-networkmanager--ifc--vlan--additional_config"></a>`additional_config`

Data type: `Hash`

Other not covered configuration
In the case when you want to specify special not listed parameters you can add them through
$additional_config hash and it will be merged with other parameters.
The additional_config has the HIGHEST priority when merged!
ie: it will override the defined values of the connection in case of the conflict
A setting with an empty string value ('') is not written, like an unset one; the connection.id, uuid, interface-name, master and slave-type can not be overridden

Default value: `{}`

## Resource types

### <a name="networkmanager_keyfile"></a>`networkmanager_keyfile`

Manages a keyfile of the NetworkManager from a hash of sections, each section is a hash of settings
(a string, a number, a boolean or an array, which is written as `a;b;`).
The `puppet resource` shows just the checksum of the content, the diffs shown by the changes have the secrets censored.
`puppet resource networkmanager_keyfile` always lists the default directory `/etc/NetworkManager/system-connections`,
whatever the `connections_dir` of the module is.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `networkmanager_keyfile` type.

##### `content`

The sections of the keyfile as a hash of hashes.

##### `ensure`

Valid values: `present`, `absent`

The basic property that the resource should be in.

Default value: `present`

##### `group`

The name of the group of the file.

Default value: `root`

##### `mode`

The octal mode of the file.

Default value: `0600`

##### `owner`

The name of the owner of the file.

Default value: `root`

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `networkmanager_keyfile` type.

* [`header`](#-networkmanager_keyfile--header)
* [`path`](#-networkmanager_keyfile--path)
* [`provider`](#-networkmanager_keyfile--provider)
* [`secret_keys`](#-networkmanager_keyfile--secret_keys)
* [`show_diff`](#-networkmanager_keyfile--show_diff)

##### <a name="-networkmanager_keyfile--header"></a>`header`

The comment written on the top of the file.

Default value: `# THIS FILE IS CONTROLLED BY PUPPET`

##### <a name="-networkmanager_keyfile--path"></a>`path`

The absolute path of the keyfile.

##### <a name="-networkmanager_keyfile--provider"></a>`provider`

The specific backend to use for this `networkmanager_keyfile` resource. You will seldom need to specify this --- Puppet
will usually discover the appropriate provider for your platform.

##### <a name="-networkmanager_keyfile--secret_keys"></a>`secret_keys`

The names of the settings whose values are censored in the diffs, in addition to the built in ones: the keys with
`password`, `passphrase`, `secret`, `private-key`, `preshared-key`, `token`, `cookie`, `credential`, `api-key` or
`auth-key` (also with `_` or without the separator) in the name, `psk`, `pin`, `wep-key0` - `wep-key3`, `mka-cak`,
`mka-ckn` and everything in the `vpn-secrets` and `secrets` sections. A name matches every setting that
contains it (case insensitive), so `key` censors all the settings with `key` in the name.

Default value: `[]`

##### <a name="-networkmanager_keyfile--show_diff"></a>`show_diff`

Valid values: `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`

Whether to show the diff of the file when it changes (with the secrets censored). The diff is shown
only when the `show_diff` setting of Puppet is enabled as well (as it is for the file resource).

Default value: `true`

### <a name="networkmanager_keyfile_dir"></a>`networkmanager_keyfile_dir`

Removes the *.nmconnection files of the directory which are not managed by a networkmanager_keyfile resource
of the catalog, when `purge` is true.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `networkmanager_keyfile_dir` type.

* [`path`](#-networkmanager_keyfile_dir--path)
* [`purge`](#-networkmanager_keyfile_dir--purge)

##### <a name="-networkmanager_keyfile_dir--path"></a>`path`

The absolute path of the directory.

##### <a name="-networkmanager_keyfile_dir--purge"></a>`purge`

Valid values: `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`

Whether to remove the *.nmconnection files which are not managed by the catalog.

Default value: `false`

### <a name="networkmanager_link"></a>`networkmanager_link`

Sets the link of the device down persistently (the device is unmanaged by NetworkManager if it can do it),
or makes the device managed by NetworkManager again after it was unmanaged by `down`.

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `networkmanager_link` type.

##### `state`

Valid values: `down`, `managed`

`down`: the link is down (with NetworkManager supporting it also unmanaged, persistently).
`managed`: the device is not unmanaged by a previous `down`, and a link which the `down` shut down with `ip`
(NetworkManager without the permanent unmanage) is brought up. A device that does not exist is in sync in both states.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `networkmanager_link` type.

* [`interface_name`](#-networkmanager_link--interface_name)
* [`mac_address`](#-networkmanager_link--mac_address)
* [`name`](#-networkmanager_link--name)
* [`provider`](#-networkmanager_link--provider)

##### <a name="-networkmanager_link--interface_name"></a>`interface_name`

The name of the network device. Either this or `mac_address` is required.

##### <a name="-networkmanager_link--mac_address"></a>`mac_address`

The MAC address of the network device (6 bytes, or 20 bytes of an InfiniBand device, the separator is a colon or a
dash), used when the `interface_name` is not set.

##### <a name="-networkmanager_link--name"></a>`name`

namevar

An arbitrary name of the resource.

##### <a name="-networkmanager_link--provider"></a>`provider`

The specific backend to use for this `networkmanager_link` resource. You will seldom need to specify this --- Puppet
will usually discover the appropriate provider for your platform.

## Functions

### <a name="networkmanager--activate_connection"></a>`networkmanager::activate_connection`

Type: Puppet Language

Activates (or deactivates, or removes) the connection after configuration

Uses $networkmanager::activation_tag (the tag of the virtual execs, collected by networkmanager::reload) and
$networkmanager::connections_dir (the directory with the keyfiles).

#### `networkmanager::activate_connection(Pattern[/\A\h{8}-(\h{4}-){3}\h{12}\z/] $uuid, String[3] $id, Enum['up', 'down'] $state, Enum['absent', 'present'] $ensure = 'present', Array[Pattern[/\A\h{8}-(\h{4}-){3}\h{12}\z/]] $after = [])`

Activates (or deactivates, or removes) the connection after configuration

Uses $networkmanager::activation_tag (the tag of the virtual execs, collected by networkmanager::reload) and
$networkmanager::connections_dir (the directory with the keyfiles).

Returns: `Any`

##### `uuid`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A\h{8}-(\h{4}-){3}\h{12}\z/]`

uuid of the connection as generated by networkmanager::connection_uuid function or supplied by user

##### `id`

Data type: `String[3]`

name of the connection (here used for a file name)

##### `state`

Data type: `Enum['up', 'down']`

the connection state

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum['absent', 'present']`

'absent' deactivates the connection before its keyfile is removed and makes NetworkManager forget it afterwards (on every run while NetworkManager still knows it, a removal which was interrupted is finished by the next run)

##### `after`

Data type: `Array[Pattern[/\A\h{8}-(\h{4}-){3}\h{12}\z/]]`

uuids of the connections (master, parent) which are activated before this one when they are managed by this module

### <a name="networkmanager--address_settings"></a>`networkmanager::address_settings`

Type: Puppet Language

Returns the keyfile settings with the IP addresses of the connection: a single address is written as `address`,
more addresses as `address1`, `address2` and so on (the format used by NetworkManager itself).
The addresses can be given as an array or as a string with the addresses separated by a semicolon.

#### `networkmanager::address_settings(Optional[Variant[String, Array[String]]] $addresses)`

Returns the keyfile settings with the IP addresses of the connection: a single address is written as `address`,
more addresses as `address1`, `address2` and so on (the format used by NetworkManager itself).
The addresses can be given as an array or as a string with the addresses separated by a semicolon.

Returns: `Hash`

##### `addresses`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String, Array[String]]]`

the address (with the prefix length) or the addresses, undef returns no settings

### <a name="networkmanager--check_ipv6_list"></a>`networkmanager::check_ipv6_list`

Type: Puppet Language

Fails when an address of the semicolon separated string is not a valid IPv6 address (with the prefix length when $cidr is true).
The arrays are validated by their data types, the legacy string format only has a rough pattern.

#### `networkmanager::check_ipv6_list(Optional[Variant[String, Array[String]]] $addresses, Boolean $cidr, String $label)`

Fails when an address of the semicolon separated string is not a valid IPv6 address (with the prefix length when $cidr is true).
The arrays are validated by their data types, the legacy string format only has a rough pattern.

Returns: `Undef`

##### `addresses`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String, Array[String]]]`

the address string or array, undef is accepted

##### `cidr`

Data type: `Boolean`

whether the prefix length is required (the addresses) or forbidden (the DNS servers)

##### `label`

Data type: `String`

the name of the parameter (for the error message)

Removes the undefined settings and the empty sections from a keyfile hash, so the caller
can list every optional setting in one literal instead of building it up conditionally.

Removes the undefined settings and the empty sections from a keyfile hash, so the caller

the module orders the activation by them).

#### `networkmanager::forbid_uuid_override(Hash $additional_config, String $id)`

on: the uuid (the connection is activated by the generated one), the id (the name of the keyfile), the interface-name
(set by the interface_name parameter), the master and the slave-type (set by the master and slave_type parameters,
the module orders the activation by them).

### <a name="networkmanager--port_settings"></a>`networkmanager::port_settings`

Type: Puppet Language

Returns the connection settings of a connection which is a port of a controller (the master): the UUID of the master
and the slave-type. NetworkManager refuses a master without the type of the controller, so the slave_type is
required when the master is set. Returns no settings without the master (the slave_type is ignored then).

#### `networkmanager::port_settings(Optional[String] $master, Optional[Networkmanager::Port_type] $slave_type, String $id)`

Returns the connection settings of a connection which is a port of a controller (the master): the UUID of the master
and the slave-type. NetworkManager refuses a master without the type of the controller, so the slave_type is
required when the master is set. Returns no settings without the master (the slave_type is ignored then).

Returns: `Hash`

##### `master`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

$id or UUID of the controller connection, undef when the connection is not a port

##### `slave_type`

Data type: `Optional[Networkmanager::Port_type]`

the type of the controller (bond, bridge, ...)

##### `id`

Data type: `String`

the id of the connection (for the error message and to refuse a master which is the connection itself)

### <a name="networkmanager--prepare_ipv4_config"></a>`networkmanager::prepare_ipv4_config`

Type: Puppet Language

Prepares the "ipv4" section of the keyfile. Only the method is written when the IPv4 is disabled,

#### `networkmanager::prepare_ipv4_config(Enum['auto', 'dhcp', 'manual', 'disabled', 'link-local'] $ipv4_method, Optional[Networkmanager::IPV4_ADDRESSES] $ipv4_address, Optional[Stdlib::IP::Address::V4::Nosubnet] $ipv4_gateway, Optional[Networkmanager::DNS_IPV4] $ipv4_dns, Boolean $ipv4_may_fail)`

the other settings would have no effect. Based on the idea of the pull request 24 by kbucheli.

##### `ipv4_method`

Data type: `Enum['auto', 'dhcp', 'manual', 'disabled', 'link-local']`

what method to use to get an IPv4 address

##### `ipv4_address`

Data type: `Optional[Networkmanager::IPV4_ADDRESSES]`

the IPv4 address(es) to assign to the interface, see networkmanager::address_settings

##### `ipv4_gateway`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::IP::Address::V4::Nosubnet]`

the IPv4 gateway for the connection

##### `ipv4_dns`

Data type: `Optional[Networkmanager::DNS_IPV4]`

the dns servers for the interface (array or semicolon separated string)

##### `ipv4_may_fail`

Data type: `Boolean`

is it OK that the IPv4 config fails?

### <a name="networkmanager--prepare_ipv6_config"></a>`networkmanager::prepare_ipv6_config`

Type: Puppet Language

Prepares the "ipv6" section of the keyfile. Only the method is written when the IPv6 is ignored or disabled,
the other settings would have no effect. Based on the idea of the pull request 24 by kbucheli.

#### `networkmanager::prepare_ipv6_config(Enum['auto', 'dhcp', 'manual', 'ignore', 'link-local', 'disabled'] $ipv6_method, Optional[Networkmanager::IPV6_ADDRESSES] $ipv6_address, Optional[Stdlib::IP::Address::V6::Nosubnet] $ipv6_gateway, Optional[Networkmanager::DNS_IPV6] $ipv6_dns, Integer[0, 3] $ipv6_addr_gen_mode, Integer[-1, 2] $ipv6_privacy, Boolean $ipv6_may_fail, Optional[String] $ipv6_dhcp_duid)`

Prepares the "ipv6" section of the keyfile. Only the method is written when the IPv6 is ignored or disabled,
the other settings would have no effect. Based on the idea of the pull request 24 by kbucheli.

Returns: `Hash`

##### `ipv6_method`

Data type: `Enum['auto', 'dhcp', 'manual', 'ignore', 'link-local', 'disabled']`

what method to use to get an IPv6 address

##### `ipv6_address`

Data type: `Optional[Networkmanager::IPV6_ADDRESSES]`

the IPv6 address(es) to assign to the interface, see networkmanager::address_settings

##### `ipv6_gateway`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::IP::Address::V6::Nosubnet]`

the IPv6 gateway for the connection

##### `ipv6_dns`

Data type: `Optional[Networkmanager::DNS_IPV6]`

the dns servers for the interface (array or semicolon separated string)

##### `ipv6_addr_gen_mode`

Data type: `Integer[0, 3]`

IPv6 method for generating of automatic interface address

##### `ipv6_privacy`

Data type: `Integer[-1, 2]`

should be the generated automatic address more private

##### `ipv6_may_fail`

Data type: `Boolean`

is it OK that the IPv6 config fails?

##### `ipv6_dhcp_duid`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

the IPv6 DHCP DUID, undef when it should not be written

### <a name="networkmanager--reload_connection"></a>`networkmanager::reload_connection`

Type: Puppet Language

Reloads the connections and changes the state of the connection through nmcli, after the NetworkManager
D-Bus service answers. The wait is limited to 60 seconds, the command fails when the service does not appear.

#### `networkmanager::reload_connection(Pattern[/\A\h{8}-(\h{4}-){3}\h{12}\z/] $uuid, Enum['up', 'down'] $state)`

Reloads the connections and changes the state of the connection through nmcli, after the NetworkManager
D-Bus service answers. The wait is limited to 60 seconds, the command fails when the service does not appear.

Returns: `String`

##### `uuid`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A\h{8}-(\h{4}-){3}\h{12}\z/]`

the connection uuid

##### `state`

Data type: `Enum['up', 'down']`

the desired connection state

### <a name="networkmanager--resolve_ipv6_duid"></a>`networkmanager::resolve_ipv6_duid`

Type: Puppet Language

Returns the IPv6 DHCP DUID to write to the keyfile of the connection, undef when nothing should be written.
The DUID is written only for the 'auto' and 'dhcp' methods of a present connection (the same in the up and the down state: it is the identity of the profile, not of its activation). The DUID of the connection wins,
the $networkmanager::ipv6_dhcp_duid_default is used when it is not set. The 'auto' DUID needs the mac address.

#### `networkmanager::resolve_ipv6_duid(Optional[Networkmanager::DHCP_DUID] $duid, Optional[Stdlib::MAC] $mac_address, String $ipv6_method, String $ensure, String $state, String $id)`

Returns the IPv6 DHCP DUID to write to the keyfile of the connection, undef when nothing should be written.
The DUID is written only for the 'auto' and 'dhcp' methods of a present connection (the same in the up and the down state: it is the identity of the profile, not of its activation). The DUID of the connection wins,
the $networkmanager::ipv6_dhcp_duid_default is used when it is not set. The 'auto' DUID needs the mac address.

Returns: `Optional[String]`

##### `duid`

Data type: `Optional[Networkmanager::DHCP_DUID]`

the DUID set for the connection (undef to use the default of the networkmanager class)

##### `mac_address`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::MAC]`

the mac address of the interface for the connection

##### `ipv6_method`

Data type: `String`

the IPv6 method of the connection

##### `ensure`

Data type: `String`

the state of the connection config

##### `state`

Data type: `String`

the state of the connection (up/down), not used

##### `id`

Data type: `String`

the id of the connection (for the error message)

### <a name="networkmanager--validate_ifc_name_and_mac"></a>`networkmanager::validate_ifc_name_and_mac`

Type: Puppet Language

Validates that the connection has at least one of 'mac address' or 'interface name' supplied

#### `networkmanager::validate_ifc_name_and_mac(String $caller, String $caller_title, Optional[Stdlib::MAC] $interface_mac, Optional[Networkmanager::Interface_name] $interface_name, String $type = 'ethernet')`

Validates that the connection has at least one of 'mac address' or 'interface name' supplied

the puppet name of the resource which called this function (for sensible error line)

##### `caller_title`

Data type: `String`

the instance of the resource which called the function (for sensible error line)

##### `interface_mac`

Data type: `Optional[Stdlib::MAC]`

the connection interface mac address

##### `interface_name`

##### `type`

Data type: `String`

the type of the connection (the section of the MAC address depends on it)

## Data types

### <a name="Networkmanager--Connection_id"></a>`Networkmanager::Connection_id`

The id of a connection, which is also used as the name of its keyfile, so it can not escape from the connections
directory or name a hidden file. Matches: not a dot first, then 1 or more printable ASCII characters (the space
included) except / and \

Alias of `Pattern[/\A(?!\.)[ -~&&[^\/\\]]+\z/]`

### <a name="Networkmanager--DHCP_DUID"></a>`Networkmanager::DHCP_DUID`

The IPv6 DHCP DUID of a connection: 'auto' builds it from the mac address of the interface (see the duid_prefix of the networkmanager class),
'unset' does not write it so NetworkManager uses its own default, the other values are the NetworkManager keywords or a literal DUID (aa:bb:cc:...)

Alias of `Variant[Pattern[/\A\h{2}(:\h{2})+\z/], Enum['auto', 'unset', 'lease', 'll', 'llt', 'stable-ll', 'stable-llt', 'stable-uuid']]`

### <a name="Networkmanager--DNS_IPV4"></a>`Networkmanager::DNS_IPV4`

Up to 5 IPv4 DNS server addresses, either as an array of addresses (eg. ['192.0.2.53', '192.0.2.54'])
or as the keyfile string with the addresses separated by a semicolon (eg. '192.0.2.53;192.0.2.54;')

Alias of `Variant[Pattern[/\A(25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])(\.(25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])){3}(;(25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])(\.(25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])){3}){0,4};?\z/], Array[Stdlib::IP::Address::V4::Nosubnet, 1, 5]]`

### <a name="Networkmanager--DNS_IPV6"></a>`Networkmanager::DNS_IPV6`

Up to 5 IPv6 DNS server addresses, either as an array of addresses (eg. ['2001:db8::53', 'fd00::1'])
or as the keyfile string with the addresses (full or compressed form) separated by a semicolon (eg. '2001:db8::53;fd00::1;').
The string has only a rough pattern here, every address of it is validated by networkmanager::check_ipv6_list.

Alias of `Variant[Pattern[/\A[[:xdigit:]:.]+(;[[:xdigit:]:.]+){0,4};?\z/], Array[Stdlib::IP::Address::V6::Nosubnet, 1, 5]]`

### <a name="Networkmanager--IPV4_ADDRESSES"></a>`Networkmanager::IPV4_ADDRESSES`

One or more IPv4 addresses with the prefix length (eg. '192.168.1.12/24', optionally followed by the gateway),
as an array or as a string with the addresses separated by a semicolon (eg. '192.168.1.12/24;192.168.2.12/24')

Alias of `Variant[Networkmanager::IPV4_CIDR, Array[Networkmanager::IPV4_CIDR, 1], Pattern[/\A(25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])(\.(25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])){3}\/([12]?[0-9]|3[0-2])(;(25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])(\.(25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])){3}\/([12]?[0-9]|3[0-2]))*;?\z/]]`

### <a name="Networkmanager--IPV4_CIDR"></a>`Networkmanager::IPV4_CIDR`

IPv4 address with the prefix length, optionally followed by a gateway (eg. '192.168.1.12/24' or '192.168.1.12/24,192.168.1.1')

Alias of `Variant[Stdlib::IP::Address::V4::CIDR, Pattern[/\A(25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])(\.(25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])){3}\/([12]?[0-9]|3[0-2]),(25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])(\.(25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])){3}\z/]]`

### <a name="Networkmanager--IPV6_ADDRESSES"></a>`Networkmanager::IPV6_ADDRESSES`

One or more IPv6 addresses with the prefix length (eg. '2001:db8::5/64'),
as an array or as a string with the addresses separated by a semicolon (eg. '2001:db8::5/64;2001:db8:1::5/64').
The string has only a rough pattern here (hex digits, colons, dots and the prefix length 0 to 128), every
address of it is validated by networkmanager::check_ipv6_list.

Alias of `Variant[Stdlib::IP::Address::V6::CIDR, Array[Stdlib::IP::Address::V6::CIDR, 1], Pattern[/\A[[:xdigit:]:.]+\/(?:[0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[01][0-9]|12[0-8])(;[[:xdigit:]:.]+\/(?:[0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|1[01][0-9]|12[0-8]))*;?\z/]]`

### <a name="Networkmanager--Interface_name"></a>`Networkmanager::Interface_name`

Name of a network device. Matches: not 'all' or 'default' (the sysctl directories of the interfaces), a letter or a
digit first (a dash would be taken as an option by ip and nmcli), then 0 to 14 printable ASCII characters except
the space, / \ : and the glob characters * ? [ ] (1 to 15 characters in total, as the kernel allows)

Alias of `Pattern[/\A(?!(all|default)\z)[0-9A-Za-z][!-~&&[^\/\\:*?\[\]]]{0,14}\z/]`

### <a name="Networkmanager--Plugin"></a>`Networkmanager::Plugin`

The name of a NetworkManager plugin (eg. 'keyfile', 'ifcfg-rh'). Matches: a lowercase letter, then lowercase
letters, digits and dashes

Alias of `Pattern[/\A[a-z][a-z0-9-]*\z/]`

### <a name="Networkmanager--Port_type"></a>`Networkmanager::Port_type`

The type of the controller of a connection which is its port (the slave-type of the keyfile): the values NetworkManager accepts
for the connection.slave-type (the alias of connection.port-type)

Alias of `Enum['bond', 'bridge', 'ovs-bridge', 'ovs-port', 'team', 'vrf']`

### <a name="Networkmanager--Unmanaged_device"></a>`Networkmanager::Unmanaged_device`

A device for the unmanaged-devices of NetworkManager.conf: a MAC address or an interface name, which may be a glob
(eg. 'docker*'). Matches: 1 to 15 printable ASCII characters except / \ : and ; (the separator of the list)

Alias of `Variant[Stdlib::MAC, Pattern[/\A[!-~&&[^\/\\:;]]{1,15}\z/]]`
